cohort: The study included preterm infants in the neonatology unit of King George's Medical University, Lucknow, U.P. India, divided into interventional and control groups (27 infants each).
finding: The premature infant oral motor intervention was effective in improving oral feeding of preterm infants, with the experimental group showing a higher mean post-interventional test score compared to the control group.
gest_age: Gestational week at birth was associated with pre-interventional feeding performance, but specific gestational age ranges for the cohort are not mentioned.
